summary: git diff shows the exact lines that changed. Use it before you commit to check what you are about to save.
notes: git diff compares your files with the staging area. git diff --staged compares the staging area with the last commit.
Lines starting with - were removed and lines starting with + were added. A changed line shows up as one of each.
The @@ line gives line numbers: -1,5 +1,5 means the 5 lines starting at line 1, before and after the change.
pitfall: git diff prints nothing after you stage your changes, so it looks like nothing changed. Use git diff --staged to see staged changes.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with one commit that has gradebook.py, README.md, and scores.csv.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
